brief: The Market Ear asks whether an AI relief rally is setting up after a liquidation. Global equity selling was heavy yesterday, net flows at -2.1 standard deviations. Long sales outpaced short sales 3 to 1, pointing to de-risking rather than shorting. The US drove 66% of global net selling, led by tech, and AI stocks saw their second-largest net selling in a year (-2.8 Z-score). Hedge funds have net sold AI stocks for five straight sessions. Goldman data shows the cumulative net buying of AI stocks since 2025's start has reversed. Net allocation to global AI stocks fell to 26.1% from a June peak of 31.7%, now at the 49th percentile, and the long/short ratio dropped from 4.34 to 3.27, in the 7th percentile. The SOX has crashed to the lower boundary of its trading range and its longer-term trend line, both held before. VXSMH, the vol gauge, has surged after weeks of complacency. The note flags CoreWeave call options, including a CRWV November $95 call that collapsed from $18 to $1 since September 8, and suggests dealer hedging unwinds amplified the selloff. It poses, without asserting, whether washed-out positioning, crushed options and oversold technicals set up a second chance.
